transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

This is likely caused by a faulty thermostat or air vent issue. You should check if the vents are blocked and ensure the temperature setting isn't too low. From what you have described, the most likely cause is food touching the cold back wall or air outlet. Food pressed against the back wall or right in front of the cold air outlet can freeze even when the fridge is at the right temperature. Was the frozen food touching the back wall or a vent (and have you moved it), or was it clear?
yeah touching the back wall near the vent slots, its rammed after big shop. havent moved it yet

First the settings: the fridge should be about 3–5°C and the freezer -18°C. Check the dial isn't on its coldest setting and that fast-freeze or super-cool hasn't been left on. Was a setting too cold or a fast-freeze / super-cool mode on (and have you changed it), or was it all set normally?
dial was on max/coldest, one of the kids prob moved it. no fast freeze or anything like that. havent changed it yet
Behind the rear panel inside the freezer, are the coils a solid block of ice, or fairly clear?
not sure how to check that, no panel inside the freezer that i know of. what do i do?

Move the food away from the back wall to stop it freezing. Check if the temperature control dial has been accidentally turned to a colder setting and adjust it back to normal. The first step is a full manual defrost: switch it off at the socket, move the food into cool bags, put towels down and leave the doors open until every bit of ice has melted, then dry it and switch it back on. Have you been able to do a full defrost, or is there no ice to clear?
no haven't defrosted, its a frost free one so i didnt think it needed it. freezer food is solid as normal. should i just turn the dial down and clear the stuff off the back?

Yes, you should move the food away from the back wall to allow air circulation and lower the thermostat setting. This will help prevent items like lettuce and yoghurt from freezing solid while maintaining proper cooling for other contents. Give it a day with the doors shut to settle at the new setting. Is the food still freezing in the fridge, or is it normal now?
did that, dial to middle and cleared the vents. after 2 days its better but one yoghurt still froze at the very back. is that normal?

It is not normal for fresh produce like lettuce and yogurt to freeze solid in a frost-free fridge. This indicates the thermostat or temperature sensor may be faulty, causing the appliance to run colder than intended despite your adjustments. Run it as normal with the doors shut for a few days. Has the frost started to build up again, or is it staying clear?
not sure, havent looked for frost tbh. its only the one yoghurt right at the back that froze so should i just keep it away from the back wall?

No, simply moving food away is not a permanent fix if the thermostat was accidentally set too low. You need to ensure the temperature control dial is correctly positioned at a medium setting and leave it there for 24 hours to stabilize. Ice in the bottom often means the defrost water can't drain away. At the bottom of the back wall there's a small drain hole — once the ice has melted, clear it gently with warm water or a soft pipe cleaner. Was the drain hole blocked (and is it clear now), is it still blocked or frozen, or was it already clear?
not sure about a drain hole, haven't looked. its only one yoghurt tho so is that fine or do i need an engineer?

It sounds like you can manage this yourself for now since it improved after adjusting the thermostat and moving food. You likely just need to ensure the vents are clear and check if the drain hole at the back of the fridge compartment is blocked, as a clog there often causes freezing issues in frost-free models. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the door being left open or a heavy load of food. Run your fingers round the rubber seal on the door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, especially where the frost is. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
